thread:
marisa: quick follow-up on the compact-slab scrubber RFC I posted earlier. can we sync on the proposed runtime behavior when the scrubber migrates subpage fragments during live inference? link: https://rfc.internal/compact-slab-scrubber

aj: skimmed it. top-level Q: scrubber move + migration = extra memcpy on critical path. do we queue migration work off the hot worker or run inline?

marisa: good Q. RFC suggests an async worker with bounded throttling so the inference path only pays a tiny tail risk when a page is actively pinned. idea is: try fast-path compaction (in-place coalesce), if that fails then enqueue migration with backpressure knobs.

kevin: +1 on async. but we need precise knobs. what are the defaults? if too aggressive we thrash PCIe and blow p99.

marisa: initial defaults we tested in perf sim: migration-rate=100 pages/s per GPU, cross-gpu-bandwidth cap=200MB/s, backoff on p99>200ms. numbers are conservative and we want canary.

rachel: can we see the sim output? we had a production incident before where background compaction collided w/ KV-cache refill and caused 15% SLO slips.

marisa: pasted a short excerpt from the sim logs: 
```
[sim] baseline p99: 185ms
[sim] scrubber aggressive (500pps): p99 up -> 312ms, avg tokens/sec -8%
[sim] scrubber conservative (100pps + 200MB/s): p99 -> 198ms, avg tokens/sec -1.2%
[sim] with KV-cache pin-protection: p99 -> 190ms
```

sam: the KV-cache pin-protection seems important. what's the API surface you want from the cache?

marisa: two lightweight ops: `pin_hint(page_id)` and `pin_release(page_id)`. scrubber checks `pin_hint` before scheduling migration. it's best-effort, not strongly blocking.

linda: ops/infra concern: pin hints need to be robust to races. if worker pins then immediately unpins we should avoid enqueueing pointless migrations. maybe we sample residency instead of strict pin checks?

aj: residency sampling + rate limiter makes sense. also add a per-tenant migration budget so noisy tenants don't starve others.

kevin: agree. also please define failure semantics: if migration fails (OOM or PCIe error), what's the rollback? we can't leave half-moved fragments.

marisa: failure flow: rollback attempt -> mark slab "sticky" for X minutes -> record telemetry metric `scrubber.migration.failures` with error and slab-id -> skip further migration until manual/auto-repair. we avoided automatic retries to prevent thundering.

ops-bot: note: add alert `scrubber.migration.fail_rate>5% for 5m` and a runbook link.

infra-bot: FYI we have a library helper `mem-migrate()` in host-utils that already does atomic switch-on-success. reuse it to avoid TOCTOU.

rachel: does mem-migrate() preserve page-level protections and KMS keys for encrypted backings? we need to be careful for Private deployments.

marisa: good catch — mem-migrate currently preserves VM mappings but not KMS-wrapped metadata. I'll add a step to copy metadata with AES-GCM tag and a fingerprint check. we'll gate that behind a flag for Private installs.

sam: rollout plan proposal: feature-flagged rollout -> traffic shadow canary (no migrations, only telemetry) -> soft enable with tenant-level budgets -> enable global but cap to 100 pages/s per-GPU -> increase as metrics look good.

aj: +1. also add a packet-capture style trace for a single migration so we can replay timings end-to-end. name it `scrubber.trace.{run_id}`.

linda: ops ask: expose the live counters in Console: `scrubber.inflight_migrations`, `scrubber.queue_depth`, `scrubber.bandwidth_used`, `scrubber.tenant_budget_util`. we want to be able to abort global if needed.

marisa: will add. also adding a lightweight tuning config in the runtime: 
```
{ "scrubber": {
    "enabled": true,
    "rate_limit_per_gpu": 100,
    "bandwidth_cap_mb_s": 200,
    "pin_protection": true,
    "tenant_budget_mb": 50
  }
}
```

kevin: tiny nit: use tokens instead of MB to avoid measuring compressed vs raw. e.g., `migration_tokens_per_minute`.

marisa: noted. we'll convert to token abstraction in the next patch.

rachel: one more operational concern: how does this interact with graceful preemption/eviction? if a migration is in-flight and eviction wants to free the slab, who wins?

marisa: priority rules: eviction > migration. eviction can cancel migration; migration must check a cancel token before commit and then abort gracefully (leave slab sticky). we'll expose `scrubber.cancel_on_evict=true` default.

sam: can we add a cheap checksum verification after migration commit? avoids silent corruption.

marisa: yes — post-migrate checksum + fingerprint. add `scrubber.verify_on_commit` flag (default true).

aj: ok actionable items: 1) marisa to update RFC with config names, failure semantics, and tenant budgeting. 2) kevin to prototype residency-sampler. 3) infra to confirm mem-migrate semantics for Private installs. 4) ops to draft alert/runbook.

linda: I'll own the Console widgets and abort toggle.

marisa: thanks all. I'll post an updated RFC patch by EOD and open a small canary PR. :thumbsup:
